# clikernel

> Use `clikernel` MCP as the default persistent Python workspace for file/notebook reads and edits, exploration, library checks, data reshaping and debugging. Imports and variables carry across calls. Read before writing, running or debugging Python with `clikernel` connected.

Base URL: https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/clikernel/

- prefer: clikernel over one-off scripts (`python -c`, heredocs); pyskills over shell (rgapi `rg` `fd` `ls`; ghapi: GitHub, git); shell: project tests, builds, non-Python tools
- outlive conversation: `create(kernel="py", autoclose=false)`, tell user its id; reply shows gateway started by this conversation: say so    /kernel needs a lasting gateway
- earlier or user's solveit kernel: `list_kernels` → `use_kernel(id)`
- `restart`: reruns that kernel's startup; redo interactive setup; `interrupt` keeps state
- `host=` names: `~/.config/clikernel/gateways.toml`; later `exec` stays on that host
- replies >`--maxout` bytes: first chunk inline + full-output temp file; `%cont` or `%cont <id>` in `exec` for next chunk; huge: `rg`/`open_doc` on temp file

### Python

- magics work, `%%bash` too; `%cd` (expands `~`), not `os.chdir`
- top-level expressions display, not those in blocks (clikernel default; startup can override)
- outputs reach conversation up to `--maxout`: `len(v)` first
- imports: once; `NameError` for your name: kernel restarted or attached: redo setup
- after `nbdev-export` or module edit: `importlib.reload`, re-import held names (`from x import y` keeps old object); `@patch` refreshes; restart only if a held instance's class changed
- loaded behavior: call it, never `inspect.getsource`    /reads disk
- before env changes, monkeypatching, extra setup: try the plain import or call

## Optional

- [clikernel.cli](cli.html.md): The stream-protocol frontend: the service on stdin/stdout for token-reading clients
- [clikernel.core](core.html.md): Gateway naming, startup delivery, and MCP sessions on jupygate gateways
- [clikernel.login](login.html.md): Sign in through a browser and save a Solveit session for gateway clients
- [clikernel.mcp](mcp.html.md): Route stdio MCP requests to jupygate gateways
- [clikernel.rules](rules.html.md): Rules that check agent-written kernel cells for common mistakes with this toolkit. The router checks each `exec` cell before forwarding it: most rules add a note to the reply, and blocking rules stop the cell. Rules see only the cell's text, not which kernel will run it, so each matches Python forms that no other kernel language produces.
